Outcome: Signal-CANdy keeps its 32-bit MCU ABI, never reuses a TX reservation generation, fails closed with SC_ERR_LIMIT after UINT32_MAX until safe state reset, and the canonical CC1A integration handles/documents that maintenance condition; all current verified edits and HIL evidence are atomically committed, Signal-CANdy dev is pushed, and exact-head CI is green. Deliverables: runtime/c99 source/header/test; application-level SC_ERR_LIMIT handling or explicit bounded integration contract in CC1A_SignalCANdy_RuntimeTest; pinned sync tooling and byte-identical firmware runtime; immutable Reports and ULW evidence; atomic commits in both repositories. Success: native RED-to-GREEN exhaustion scenario proves no mutation and reset recovery; installed Fantomas, managed/native/sanitizer/hardening gates pass; deterministic G474 firmware is TT_Host-only flashed and NI CAN3 HIL prints 35 PASS plus ALL PASS with cleanup receipts; exact pushed Signal-CANdy head passes CI and final independent code/QA/gate review. Constraints: preserve uint32 public ABI and 32-bit MCU performance; no uint64 generation; allocation-free bounded C99; preserve SCIMG v1 and AOT behavior; ST-Link/SWD forbidden; exact claimed CC1A-Test-1/COM22/NI CAN3/TT_Host 9802 only; retain the single CC1A claim; do not modify GAS_BSP or GAS_SDP private source; sibling has no remote so commit only. assumed: exhaustion is a maintenance/reset condition rather than automatic runtime reset — reset requires a quiescent application boundary and is reversible. WHEN TO STOP: stop right away when every criterion is receipt-backed on frozen committed trees, both repositories are clean except unrelated pre-existing files, Signal-CANdy origin/dev exact-head CI is green, final quality gate approves, and the aggregate checkpoint is complete.
